title: Platform scrimshaw — control plane / routing / auth / quotas standup notes 2027-11-29
content:
Context and purpose:
This is the weekly rapid standup capture for the ad-hoc 'Scrimshaw' cohort — short sync focused on control plane, routing, auth, and quotas. We intentionally keep it lightweight: decisions, short-term actions, and open questions.

Attendees (11/29):
- Aisha (owner)
- Marco (routing)
- Liang (auth)
- Renee (quotas)
- Tom (SRE, on call) — joined for incident notes
- Carmen (observer, infra rotation)

Agenda (10 min):
1) Quick scoreboard (alerts / regressions)
2) Routing experiment / canary status
3) Auth token renewal and error spike
4) Quotas math & emergency throttle thresholds
5) Immediate action items + owners

Quick scoreboard / health:
- No p95 latency SLO breaches in the last 24h for the control plane, but a minor p50 spike (200ms->320ms) between 03:12–03:26 UTC attributed to AZ B transient throttling (investigating).
- Quotas service emitted a burst of quota-evaluation-failures (~120) when large batch job from internal analytics hit the platform at 04:05 UTC. Root cause seems to be a thin cache window + GC pause on the node running rate-limiter-worker-3.
- Auth: token-validation errors spiked to 0.4% for 18 minutes. Errors were 401/invalid_signature from a subset of gateway tokens; rollout of jwt-lib v2.7.1 (hotfix) fixed it.

Notes by area:
1) Control plane (Aisha)
- Control plane rollout for multi-region routing (PLT-9876) progressed: canary 1 -> 2 -> rollback on 2 due to unexpected stale-route reads. We rolled back Canary2 and throttled new rollouts.
- Action: add a read-after-update consistency check to the controlplane state write path (pre-commit hook). Ticket created: PLT-10111. Owner: Aisha. ETA: EOW (2027-12-03) for prototype.
- Observability gap: we still lack a route-diff metric that surfaces stale reads (how often local caches return version older than controlplane head). Marco to propose metric name + tags.

2) Routing (Marco)
- Route selection A/B experiment (per-customer policy preference) is live in canary for 5% traffic. Early metrics: fallthrough rate decreased by 16%, but tail latency for routed fallbacks increased ~30ms.
- We're seeing intermittent increase in cross-region hops when the fallback policy triggers; hypothesis: route preference table TTL too short causing frequent recompute.
- Short-term fix: bump route-pref TTL from 45s -> 180s in canary. Marco to push change and monitor. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1893.
- Long-term: plan to implement sticky routing tokens (design doc draft in Confluence).

3) Auth (Liang)
- Incident: jwt-lib v2.7.0 introduced stricter header parsing; some older gateway tokens signed by legacy key provider failed. We hotfixed by rolling out v2.7.1 with backward-compat shim.
- Action: add a compatibility test to the auth integration suite that validates each gateway token variant we still accept. Ticket: PLT-9944. Owner: Liang. ETA: 2027-12-06.
- We need to upstream a small patch to gateway key distributer to add explicit key-version header to tokens. Rafael will own the gateway change (out of auth team).

4) Quotas (Renee)
- The quotas burst on analytics job exposed two weak points: (a) rate-limiter-worker node affinity (single AZ) and (b) cache TTL interplay with large batch re-evals.
- Immediate mitigation: increase concurrency cap for rate-limiter-worker pool (worker-5 -> worker-8) and schedule analytics batch to off-peak window (ops to coordinate).
- Action: create multi-AZ affinity for rate-limiter-workers and shrink local cache window from 120s -> 30s with a small burst-tolerant backoff. Ticket: PLT-10202. Owner: Renee. ETA: 2027-12-10.

Incident follow-up (Tom):
- On-call recorded that the GC pauses correlated with a new JVM memory bump in the image used by worker-3. Rolling image back to previous tag eliminated pauses in a canary test. We need a safer rollout gating for worker JVM images.
- Action: implement a canary roll for worker images with GC latency smoke-test. Owner: Tom. ETA: 2027-12-07.

Metrics snapshot (quick numbers taken 11/29 09:00 UTC):
- Control plane p95: 42ms, p99: 310ms (one noisy sample), p50: 18ms.
- Routing fallthrough rate (canary): 3.4% vs baseline 4.1%.
- Auth error rate (post-hotfix): stabilized to 0.02%.
- Quotas eval error count (24h): 17 -> post-mitigation target < 3/day.

Decisions made:
- Rollout cadence: stop automatic progression from Canary2 -> Canary3 until read-after-update check is in place (PLT-10111).
- Route-pref TTL bumped in canary to 180s as an interim measure (monitor for tail-latency regressions).
- Schedule analytics heavy jobs to run 0200–0500 UTC where possible; ops to notify analytics team and add guardrail.

Action items (owner / due):
- Aisha: prototype read-after-update check + add route-diff metric proposal. Due: 2027-12-03.
- Marco: push TTL bump to canary (PR linked), monitor tail latency, report 24h after rollout. Due: 2027-11-30.
- Liang: compatibility tests for gateway token variants (PLT-9944). Due: 2027-12-06.
- Renee: start multi-AZ worker affinity ticket (PLT-10202) and schedule concurrency increase. Due: 2027-12-10.
- Tom: worker image canary gate + GC smoke-test. Due: 2027-12-07.
- Ops (TBD): coordinate analytics team for off-peak window, add scheduling guardrail.

Parking lot / open questions:
- Do we need a global sequence number for route table updates to make stale detection easier? (this would be heavier lift)
- Is the current throttling model (burst tokens + leaky bucket) still the best for large internal batch jobs or do we need a separate throttler for internal service accounts?
- How much telemetry cost are we willing to accept for per-route diff metrics? Need product input.

Notes to self / meeting micro-notes:
- Try a small synthetic load test that simulates analytics job concurrency pattern (10K evals in 3s window) against staging quotas endpoint.
- Remember to include examples of legacy gateway token in the auth test vectors repo.
- Add an automated smoke script to the controlplane CI that fails the build if stale read probability > 0.1% on synthetic run.

Next sync: quick check-in Fri 12/03 10:00 UTC (or async updates in the thread). If any action (esp PLT-10111) slips, escalate to platform leads.

End of notes.
